Soil Description: Moist, rich soils such as clay loam or sandy loam suit this plant.
Flowers appear in early summer.

Bloom Color: Yellow

Native Habitat: Rocky slopes and limestone ledges.

Water Use: Low
Height: Up to about 3 feet tall.
Fruit: Small brown capsule
Leaf: Gray-green and narrow.
Gardeners report that it thrives in wet, mucky clay and makes a good choice for pond margins.

Family: Ericaceae
Duration: Perennial
Habit: Shrub
Leaf Retention: Deciduous, the leaves turning red in autumn.
